title: Sixkey Phase 1 sync: shared known-answer vectors (M0)
source: docs/SYNC-DESIGN.md (revision 15; the M0 notes N0-N29 are resolved in §0.0d and §0.0e, the M1 review in §0.0f, the M4 backend review in §0.0o; enrolment v2 and the pairing code: revision 27, §0.0aa). Remaining observations: contract/M0-NOTES.md.

base64url.rule: RFC 4648 §5 alphabet, no padding. Decoding is strict: reject padding, other characters, length % 4 == 1, and any string that does not re-encode to itself (non-canonical trailing bits). §2.2 (§0.0d N19).

decode_reject.why: non-canonical trailing bits (canonical form of 00 is AA)
non-canonical trailing bits (canonical form of 0000 is AAA)

base64.rule: RFC 4648 §4 alphabet with padding, Phase 0 fromB64 rules: length % 4 == 0 and /^[A-Za-z0-9+/]*={0,2}$/.

decode_accept_noncanonical.why: non-canonical trailing bits are accepted by Phase 0 fromB64 (atob); M0 keeps that behaviour for standard base64

canonical_json.section: §2.2 KeyBundle MAC input, §3.2 M5 payload P, §3.9 P2
canonical_json.rule: Phase 0 canonicalJson (core/vault/merge.ts): keys sorted by UTF-16 code units, undefined members dropped, primitives as JSON.stringify. Cross-language stable only for strings, booleans, null and safe integers (Python: json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False)). §2.3, §5.4 (§0.0d N20): every number is a safe integer; see number_tokens.

time_truncation.rule: floor to the UTC hour/day/minute of the ms Unix timestamp: floor(ms / 3600000) * 3600000. Postgres date_trunc on timestamptz uses the session TimeZone, so the migration sets ALTER ROLE sixkey_api SET timezone = 'UTC'. §2.3, §5.3 (§0.0d N4).

padding.rule: append ASCII spaces (0x20) to the UTF-8 plaintext until its length is a multiple of 16384; a plaintext already at a multiple gets no bytes (§4.1, §0.0d N23). JSON.parse ignores the trailing whitespace.

vk_subkeys.rule: HKDF-SHA256(VK, salt = empty, info = label), 256 bits except vk-id (64 bits, lowercase hex). §2.2 (§0.0d N3): every HKDF output is 256 bits except vk-id; HMAC keys are derived with an explicit length of 256 (WebCrypto's HMAC deriveKey without a length gives 512 bits and a different MAC, kept as a counterexample in keybundle.mac_cases).

webcrypto_hazard.note: deriveKey(HKDF -> AES-256-GCM, extractable) exported equals deriveBits(256) for the same info. This is why every label must differ: with one label, K_write (sent to the server) would equal K_enc.

envelope.note: Unpadded plaintext to keep the file small; real uploads pad first (padding group). The envelope travels and is stored as this exact JSON text; head = SHA-256 of its UTF-8 bytes, standard base64.

head_of_reserialized_text.note: same object, different text: different head. The server hashes the raw text it stores.

write_proof.rule: K_write = HKDF(VK, empty, 'sixkey/v1/vault-write', 256), sent as write_key / new_write_key (standard base64). write_proof = HMAC-SHA256(K_write, UTF-8('sixkey-write|1|{vaultId}|{if_version}|{envelope.checksum}')), standard base64. if_version is decimal; the checksum is the envelope's standard-base64 checksum field verbatim.

recovery_auth.rule: recAuth = HKDF(secret128, empty, 'sixkey/v1/recovery-auth', 256), sent as recovery_auth (standard base64). recovery_verifier = SHA-256(UTF-8('sixkey-recovery-verifier|1|') || recAuth raw 32 bytes), standard base64.
equivalent_inputs: M2GT 58X4 MPKA FA59 NANT SBDE NX83

contrast.note: These must all differ from recovery_auth / recovery_verifier: the server learns recAuth, which must not open the recovery wrap.

password_auth.rule: pw_auth = HKDF(PBKDF2-SHA256(UTF-8(NFKC(pw)), salt_auth, iterations, 256 bits), empty, 'sixkey/v1/password-auth', 256 bits), sent as password_auth (standard base64). password_verifier = SHA-256(UTF-8('sixkey-password-verifier|1|') || pw_auth raw 32 bytes), standard base64. salt_auth and iterations come from KeyBundle.auth.kdf and must differ from the password wrap's salt.

kdf_params.note: Read-time bounds (Phase 0 core/crypto/kdf.ts assertKdfParams, enforced again by §3.14): 600000 <= iterations <= 20000000, salt >= 16 bytes, v 1, hash SHA-256.

keybundle.rule: mac = base64(HMAC-SHA256(K_mac, UTF-8('sixkey-keybundle|1|' + canonicalJson(bundle without mac)))), K_mac = HKDF(VK, empty, 'sixkey/v1/keybundle-mac', 256). The bundle travels and is stored as raw JSON text; receivers parse generically and keep unknown fields. Time fields (at, wraps[].createdAt, previous[].createdAt) are truncated to the hour before upload (T1).

number_tokens.rule: Every number in a KeyBundle, the enrollment payload and every request body is a safe integer written as an integer literal: no fraction, no exponent, |n| <= 2^53 - 1. The server rejects any other number token with 422 invalid_request. The check is on the raw text: JSON.parse turns 3.0, 1.7920512e12 and 6e5 into integers, so a check on parsed values would miss them (same_value_after_json_parse). Python: json.loads with parse_float and parse_constant raising and parse_int range-checked.

device_name.rule: §2.4 (§0.0d N5): NFKC; trim U+0020 at both ends; then reject, in this order: not_well_formed (lone surrogate), empty, too_long (> 40 code points, not UTF-16 units), control_char (General_Category Cc), bidi_control (U+061C, U+200E-200F, U+202A-202E, U+2066-2069), zero_width (U+200B-200D, U+2060, U+FEFF). UTF-8, right-pad with 0x20 to exactly 160 bytes; decoding strips trailing 0x20, which now round-trips exactly. name_ct = {vkId, iv, ct} with ct = AES-256-GCM(K_name(VK), padded, AAD 'sixkey-devname|1|{vaultId}|{vkId}|{deviceId}'), so ct is always 176 bytes (236 base64 chars).

enrollment.rule: Enrolment v2 (revision 27). C = SHA-256(UTF-8(commit_input)); h = SHA-256(UTF-8(T)); Z = ECDH(esk, peer epk), 32 bytes; S = the approver's 16-byte pairing secret (shown as pairing_code, typed on the new device before reveal, never sent); K = HKDF(IKM = Z || S, salt = h, 'sixkey/v2/enroll-key', 256); SAS = uint32be(SHA-256(UTF-8('sixkey/v2/enroll-sas|') || h raw)[0..4]) mod 10^6, zero-padded to 6 digits. There is no confirmation code. In T and in the AADs every byte field is base64url without padding; in request bodies they are standard base64. rid is the lowercase hyphenated UUID. payload and the reveal name_ct travel as standard base64 of iv(12) || ciphertext || tag(16) (§3.2, §0.0d N6); the reveal name is padded to 160 bytes first, so its wire value is 188 bytes (§2.4, §0.0d N5).

mitm.note: The server runs two sessions: toward N it answers with its own epk (N computes h1), toward A it reveals its own epk and nonce, committed in a substituted C' (A computes h2). Every enrolment ciphertext is under K = HKDF(Z || S, h), so without the pairing secret S the server can make neither a reveal name_ct that A opens (A ends with pairing_mismatch, before the SAS step) nor a payload that N opens (N ends with bad_payload): 2^-128 each. If S has leaked, it must still make SAS(h1) == SAS(h2) to pass A (10^-6, one guess per request); toward N there is no second check (§1.3, §10 row 110).

label_swap.note: The check bits are domain-separated (§3.2 MUST 10): the same 16 bytes as a recovery code (first 12 bits of SHA-256(S), no tag) and as a pairing code (SHA-256(UTF-8('sixkey-pairing-code|1|') || S)) differ in their check bits, so each is rejected where the other belongs (about 1 in 4096 would slip through for some other secret).

sas.rule: SAS = uint32be(SHA-256(UTF-8('sixkey/v2/enroll-sas|') || h)[0..4]) mod 10^6 (enrolment v2, revision 27). h is the raw 32-byte transcript hash. The value is the 6-digit zero-padded decimal string; the UI shows it as two groups of 3. The new device shows it, the approver types it (3 tries). There is no confirmation code since revision 27.

pairing_code.rule: The pairing code shows the 16-byte pairing secret S like a recovery code: n = S (128 bits) << 12 | check, where check = the first 12 bits of SHA-256(UTF-8('sixkey-pairing-code|1|') || S); 28 Crockford base32 symbols (0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ), most significant first, shown as 7 groups of 4 joined by '-'. Reading: upper-case, drop whitespace, '-' and '_', read O as 0 and I and L as 1; then not 28 symbols is pairing_length, a symbol outside the alphabet pairing_char, wrong check bits pairing_checksum. All three are local (no attempt used, no state change); a recovery code is rejected by its check bits.

request_signature.rule: input = 'sixkey-req|1|{host}|{METHOD}|{target}|{signer}|{sub}|{ts}|{base64url(SHA-256(body bytes))}'. host = configured API host (URL.host: lowercase, port only when non-default); target = raw request target (path + query, verbatim, never containing '|'); signer = deviceId or 'enroll:{rid}'; sub = JWT sub when the request carries an account session, else '-'; ts = the Sixkey-Ts header (decimal ms). No body = SHA-256 of zero bytes. Signature: ECDSA P-256 / SHA-256, IEEE P1363 r||s (64 bytes), base64url in Sixkey-Sig. The server converts to DER for verification.

fork_signature.rule: POST /v1/devices/fork carries two signatures over ONE signing input (the normal one, with the current deviceId as signer): Sixkey-Sig by the current DSK, verified with the device row's key, and Sixkey-New-Sig by the new private key, verified with the body's new_sig_pubkey. Both headers are base64url P1363 (64 bytes). The body has no new_sig member. A missing or wrong Sixkey-New-Sig is 401 bad_signature.

rotate_repair.rule: Repair is a rotate that does not change this device's VK: the server was rolled back to the state of the envelope and keybundle groups (VK1, kver 3), while this device holds VK2 and keyring2 (previous contains VK1). envelope and bundle.keyring use VK2 and may differ from the server's vk_id; if_version / if_kver are the server's values and bundle.kver = publishKver(server kver, maxSeenKver) = min(max(3, 6) + 1, 3 + KVER_MAX_JUMP) = 7 (§3.9 R1, §0.0e N27, §0.0f F-01); write_proof uses K_write of VK1 (the server's current write_key); new_write_key is K_write of VK2; password_auth follows the rolled-back bundle's auth.kdf; recovery_verifier is required and comes from a recovery code the user types (or a new one), since the device never stores the code (I9); password_verifier uses the new auth salt.

keys_repair.rule: Same-VK repair through PUT /v1/keys: the server's bundle went back (keybundle group, VK1, kver 3) while this device holds a newer VK1 keyring (new password and recovery wraps) and saw kver 6, so it is in keys_behind. It republishes its own keyring with if_kver = the server's kver and bundle.kver = publishKver(3, 6) = min(max(3, 6) + 1, 3 + KVER_MAX_JUMP) = 7 (a jump, accepted because if_kver < kver <= if_kver + KVER_MAX_JUMP). No write proof. password_auth follows the server's current bundle; recovery_verifier comes from a recovery code the user types; password_verifier is required because the password wrap and auth.kdf changed (P4).
keys_repair.p4_rule: P4 (§2.3, §0.0f S-2), keyless, server and client alike: the recovery wrap changed <=> recovery_verifier is required; the password wrap changed <=> auth.kdf changed <=> password_verifier is required; otherwise 422 invalid_request. A wrap changed when its iv or its wrapped bytes did; createdAt and every other member are ignored.

kver_rules.rule: Publish: kver = publishKver(server kver, maxSeenKver) = min(max(server kver, maxSeenKver) + 1, server kver + KVER_MAX_JUMP); a result that is not a safe integer is the error kver_overflow and nothing is published. Server: the app layer accepts only if_kver < kver <= if_kver + KVER_MAX_JUMP, else 422 invalid_request; the CAS is on if_kver; a failed CAS whose stored bundle text equals the submitted text is the idempotent 200, otherwise 409 keys_conflict. Adoption (R0/R1, only MAC- and vaultId-verified bundles are classified): kver > maxSeenKver may be adopted (R2/R3 still apply; maxSeenKver = kver afterwards), except that when maxSeenKver > 0 a kver above maxSeenKver + KVER_MAX_JUMP counts as kver <= maxSeenKver (it cannot raise maxSeenKver); kver <= maxSeenKver with the same keyring (canonicalJson) is in sync and maxSeenKver stays; with a different keyring it is keys_behind: not adopted, no 'take the server's' action, the only way out is repairing the cloud from this device, and R3 asks for confirmation before an old password may adopt it. Bundles are referenced by group: keybundle = the server's rolled-back bundle (kver 3), keys_repair = the repaired bundle (kver 7); a facts_only case uses the bundle only for its content and classifies the given bundle_kver. §3.9 (§0.0e N27, §0.0f F-01).
